explanation: Protists were historically classified under a single kingdom because they were thought to be monophyletic. However, DNA evidence has shown that all protists do not evolve from a single common ancestor, revealing instead six distinct evolutionary lines. Eukaryotes, including protists, are therefore grouped into Supergroups, which represent taxonomic levels below domain but above kingdom, each representing a separate evolutionary lineage. The six supergroups are Archaeplastida, Chromalveolata, Excavata, Amoebozoa (Amoebazoan), Opisthokonta (Opisthokontan), and Rhizaria.

questions.q: What taxonomic rank represents a level below Domain but above Kingdom?
questions.exp: The notes state that Supergroups are a 'Level below domain but above kingdom'.

questions.q: Why was the kingdom-level classification of all protists in a single group abandoned?
opts: DNA evidence showed they do not evolve from a single common ancestor.
They were found to be multicellular prokaryotes.
They were merged with the kingdom of viruses.
questions.exp: DNA evidence disproved their monophyletic status by showing that protists do not all evolve from a single common ancestor.
